scope: Read-only source/dependency review of 19 exact residual entries for the accepted Linux production candidate. No model access, builds, runtime tests, baseline edit or release promotion. Source hashes bind entire files containing inspected boundary excerpts; they do not imply every line was audited.

components.risk: Moderate: byte-level decoder and string-validity invariants on key material.
components.boundary: In-place base64 decoding uses overlapping-source/destination raw pointers; encoding converts known ASCII output with unchecked UTF-8. No external FFI.
components.justification: The full-chunk loop derives 4-byte reads and 3-byte writes from buf.len()/4 and reads into a temporary before writing. The remainder derives lengths from the decoded length, rejects invalid encodings, then copies from a separate fixed-size temporary. Encoders bound destination size and emit the fixed base64 alphabet/padding, which supports the unchecked UTF-8 conversion. The crate warns on unsafe_code and locally allows these operations; it does not forbid them. This dependency remains necessary for strict PKCS key/PEM handling after removal of RustCrypto rsa.
components.residual_risk: Arithmetic and alphabet invariants still depend on this exact upstream implementation. Source review did not fuzz malformed or extreme-length inputs, prove constant-time behavior, or establish that every exported method is called by the executable.

inventory_metric.meaning: Absence of the unconditional forbid marker is an inventory indicator, not an unsafe operation count or a memory safety verdict.

components.risk: High: ownership and lifetime bridge around platform cryptography objects.
components.boundary: foreign_type! generates raw foreign pointers, owning Drop, pointer-to-reference Deref/DerefMut and optional clone hooks.
components.justification: Owned handles delegate destruction to the specified C destructor; borrowed references are tied by generated Deref to the Rust wrapper borrow. Correctness therefore requires non-null live objects, matched allocation/free functions, and valid aliasing supplied by openssl. The macro does not itself validate arbitrary pointers; from_ptr is unsafe. Review of openssl null-result conversion and RAII call sites supports the selected integration rather than treating this macro as intrinsically safe.
components.residual_risk: A mismatched destructor, invalid pointer, C-side aliasing or refcount error can cause UB. Type definitions and C-library behavior remain part of the trusted boundary; the entire openssl object catalog was not audited.

components.risk: High: cryptographic C ABI, opaque-object ownership, I/O callbacks and secret operations.
components.boundary: Safe Rust wrappers call the platform OpenSSL C library for TLS and RSA3072/SHA256 identity operations. Selected paths include RSA allocation/key generation, EVP signing, DER parsing/serialization, SSL read/write and BIO callbacks.
components.justification: Inspected cvt_p/cvt reject null/nonpositive C returns before safe wrappers are formed; RSA generation obtains a managed handle before the fallible operation. Sign-to-Vec allocates the advertised output size and truncates to actual output. MemBioSlice retains a lifetime marker for borrowed input and checks C integer length bounds. TLS calls pass Rust buffer lengths; BIO callbacks catch Rust panics before crossing the C boundary. The Susi Linux provider itself forbids unsafe_code, validates PKCS8 and RSA consistency, signs through EVP, and verifies using an exported/reimported public key. These checks justify the selected boundary, while not eliminating the C dependency.
components.residual_risk: Correct C lengths, ownership/refcounts, thread behavior, ABI/header matching and cryptographic behavior remain trusted. This is not a full audit of the large openssl crate or system library and does not prove constant-time behavior. Qualification must separately bind the actual dynamic library/provider and keep advisory/TLS gates enabled; upgrades require requalification.

components.risk: High: compressed-input parser using manually managed allocation and unchecked byte copies.

components.risk: High: self-referential allocation, erased dependent lifetimes and manual drop order.
components.boundary: Macro-generated cell places owner and borrowing dependent in stable heap storage; UnsafeSelfCell erases pointers/lifetimes and reconstructs borrows, Send/Sync and destruction.
components.justification: Inspected invariants require initialized immovable owner, stable allocation, controlled access and dependent-before-owner destruction. Constructors take a higher-ranked builder borrowing only the owner; panic guards free initialized state, and explicit drop order avoids dangling dependent destructors. Send/Sync require the corresponding owner/dependent traits. The selected candle-core use is covariant SafeTensors borrowing either Vec<u8> or mmap ownership, with no old_rust feature enabled; the documented pre-1.51 fallback is not selected.
components.residual_risk: Macro expansion, variance and destructor/panic paths remain subtle. For mmap-backed tensors, file mutation/truncation is a separate unsafe mmap caller obligation which self_cell does not solve. This review did not exercise models or establish file immutability; it preserves that existing API obligation.

components.risk: High: task Context lifetime and manual Send/Sync across asynchronous TLS polling.
components.boundary: AllowStd stores a raw erased Context pointer while adapting AsyncRead/AsyncWrite to native-tls synchronous calls; with_context casts it back. Send/Sync are manually conditioned on the stream traits.
components.justification: Inspected stream polling installs the current Context, uses a Guard to clear it on completion/unwind, asserts it is non-null before access, and converts Pending to WouldBlock. Initial handshake code clears the pointer before returning either completed or resumable handshake state. Exclusive &mut access and S: Unpin support the temporary pin/borrow. This confines the raw context to polling rather than persisting a valid Rust reference across awaits.
components.residual_risk: The invariants still depend on all handshake/panic/reentrancy paths, native-tls callback behavior and correct stream trait implementations. No complete concurrency model check was run. Native provider risks remain additional to this pointer-lifetime bridge.

components.risk: High: interpreter validity, raw instruction/stack pointers and pinned code lifetime.
components.boundary: Interpreter internals use raw instruction pointers and unchecked indexing assumptions from validated translation; CodeMap extends references to pinned append-only code beyond its mutex guard. Memory growth refreshes cached pointers.
components.justification: The reviewed Module::new path parses and validates; Susi calls it after size checks and does not invoke Module::new_unchecked. The selected extra-checks feature makes the interpreter unreachable_unchecked macro panic rather than invoke core::hint::unreachable_unchecked, while other raw pointer operations remain. Susi limits modules to 64 MiB, each store to one memory/instance/table, memory to 256 MiB, table elements to 1,000,000, output to 16 MiB and fuel to 10,000,000. CodeMap lifetime adjustment documents pinned append-only storage. These are concrete mitigations for model-written Wasm, not evidence the interpreter is memory-safe by construction.
components.residual_risk: Translator bugs can invalidate instruction/stack pointer assumptions; pinned-lifetime and cache invalidation correctness remain trusted. Fuel/resource caps do not guarantee memory safety or total compile-time CPU bounds. This scoped review is not a full interpreter audit or new adversarial/fuzz campaign.

components.risk: Low to moderate: transparent string wrapper and thread-trait bounds for arenas.
components.boundary: LenOrderStr converts &str using transmute; Arena/ComponentVec implement Send/Sync without requiring the phantom index type to be Send/Sync.

This is the precise residual unsafe surface, distinct from the larger interpreter.
components.residual_risk: Correctness assumes no later interior state is added without updating trait bounds and the transparent wrapper layout remains unchanged. This does not validate the interpreter algorithms consuming these collections.
